correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact 2020 criterion for \(2^a p\), coprime multiplier closure, and a CRT square witness \(1\le x\le 2^a p^2\) to get a positive Zumkeller complement whenever \(N>15376^2\). The \(p^2\) local set has exactly (p-1)(p+2)/2 elements by root lifting, and four disjoint binary strata have measures 1/2,1/8,1/8,1/4. Their independent odd-prime coordinates yield the exact rational 63520442937841228526/83108492151210387225. Finite verification checked all local prime residues, the exact rational calculation, all 44100 residues in a three-prime CRT case and fifty sampled constructive witnesses. The abstract infinite inclusion does not rely on experiments.

originality.rationale: Somu, Kukla, Tran (2023) Proposition 4.11 gives ten of eighteen classes, namely density \(5/9\), but not the additional p-square conditions or the 0.764307... finite-sieve density. Their Theorem 4.17 proves infinitely many failures, and Conjecture 4.21 predicts density zero for the failures; neither yields the new quantitative bound. Mahanta, Saikia, Yaqubi (2020) gives the crucial \(2^a p\) divisor criterion but no additive density. The 2023 paper also treats Zumkeller-plus-prime representations, which do not imply square representations. Targeted record and literature searches returned no equivalent stronger theorem. The possibility of an unindexed or implicitly known sieve remains.
residual_risks: No claim of global uniqueness: an unindexed or differently phrased earlier density computation may exist.
Theorem is only a lower density certificate, not an exact density formula for the entire sumset.
Originality could be reduced if a general quantitative periodic-cover theorem already explicitly subsumes these same congruence classes; no such dominating statement appeared in checked sources.

value.rationale: The motivating 2023 paper proves only an eventually represented set of 10 modulo-18 classes (density \(5/9\)) and asks in Conjecture 4.21 whether the exceptions have density zero. The theorem gives a strictly stronger, explicit 76.43% lower asymptotic bound and supplies a systematic ten-prime congruence certificate, plus a uniform constructive cutoff. This is a nontrivial quantitative partial answer, while not settling the conjecture or claiming sharpness.
